requirements.requirement: Deploy and confirm a healthy 3-member Galera cluster (node1/node2/node3) holding application data before the maintenance window
requirements.summary: Cluster bootstrapped on node1 and joined sequentially by node2 and node3 with wsrep_cluster_size growing 1->2->3 and status Primary/ready (cmd-1489ce9446c34f58, cmd-7225369a201e4736, cmd-cfb2077413b54fa6, cmd-67963372023a4327, cmd-4389b52efba44330, cmd-41ba202617f04907). appdb.orders created and 3 rows inserted on node1, then confirmed byte-identical on node2 and node3 (cmd-b8d7235532614236, cmd-c1ce6156482c4b12, cmd-96c846a5c506406f), establishing the pre-maintenance healthy baseline directly.

requirements.requirement: Bring the entire cluster down completely for a maintenance window
requirements.summary: node3, node2, then node1 stopped in that order via systemctl stop mariadb (cmd-d8386408d78c499e, cmd-c22e8f33dc124e25, cmd-591dfb48bc95420e), with node1's grastate.dat showing safe_to_bootstrap:1/seqno:11 confirming the last node stopped cleanly. systemctl is-active on all three nodes immediately after returns 'inactive' simultaneously (cmd-fb9bf8025cb0412b, cmd-243c203a78c14959, cmd-58713df98c1d40c6), directly demonstrating a full, bounded cluster-wide outage.

requirements.requirement: Bring the cluster back with every committed write still present and all three members serving again
requirements.summary: node1 re-bootstrapped via galera_new_cluster (seeded from its saved seqno 11 state), then node2 and node3 rejoined via SST, restoring wsrep_cluster_size to 3/Primary (cmd-937f1475d6774c03, cmd-9113ef89894e4ee8, cmd-fb37119629974f89). All 3 pre-shutdown rows verified identical on all three nodes post-restart (cmd-8a35dd5ad91a4bf7, cmd-3fd7c89c438d4e57, cmd-c22d75827dd74f1d), and a new post-maintenance write from node2 was confirmed replicated and counted correctly on node1 and node3 (cmd-3f64d71e3c224cf5, cmd-0a434aea19514814, cmd-d07cda52e6ae423a), directly proving no data loss and full read/write availability across all three members.

requirements.requirement: Cluster remains consistent and fully served across all nodes after all individual restarts complete
requirements.summary: After all three sequential node reboots, all three nodes independently report cluster_size 3, local_state Synced, and byte-identical 4-row appdb.orders datasets (cmd-ba3ea53f5b0a4ea4, cmd-4f96fd8be0254790, cmd-85bf43e6c4b84308).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task contract are directly and coherently demonstrated: a healthy 3-member Galera cluster with application data was established, the cluster was brought down completely for the maintenance window (all three nodes simultaneously inactive), and it was restored afterward with all pre-shutdown rows intact plus a verified new post-maintenance write replicating correctly, proving full read/write recovery across all three members. The independently mandated node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for each node in turn, with baseline health, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered cluster/data state all directly observed and cross-checked against the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshots, which match the executor-reported values exactly.
limitations: mariadb bind-address was set to 0.0.0.0 on all nodes, broadening network exposure beyond what strict Galera intra-cluster replication alone requires; this is common for an app-serving database cluster given the '%'-host appuser grant, but was not independently verified against any firewall/security-group layer in the captured evidence.

No prepare-phase snapshot distinct from before_prepare was available (prepare disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the executor's own before/after actions rather than a distinct prepare baseline.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the full chronological command trace. All state-changing commands map cleanly to setup (package install, galera config), the required maintenance shutdown/restart, application data creation, or the mandated per-node restart protocol. The generated appuser password was written to a temp file and explicitly deleted immediately after use (cmd-6f8c93d2fa1841e4, cmd-6bd59ee8c0314318), leaving no residue. No abandoned files, failed services, or conflicting mutations were observed; after_executor snapshots show empty failed-services lists on all three nodes and only expected transient systemd-private tmp dirs tied to the new boot session. One minor note: bind-address=0.0.0.0 was applied on all three nodes (visible in the after_executor listening-sockets diff, port 3306 now 0.0.0.0), broadening MySQL client exposure beyond node-to-node Galera ports; this is a common/expected pattern for an app-serving cluster with a '%'-host appuser grant, not an unbounded or clearly unnecessary mutation, so it is noted as a minor limitation rather than a scored hygiene violation.
